description: The hand-verified expected result for the negative Joern fixture whose defect is structural: one element of findings[] that is not an object at all, while the enclosing document stays well-formed JSON. Every value was derived by reading the fixture and the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/ -- emit.FIELDS for the field set and order, paths.REJECT_CLASSES for the class name, the adapter's documented five-step classification order for the step each record is decided at, and severity.py's no-vocabulary path for the severity triple. The adapter was run afterwards, to corroborate, never to source these values. Where this file and harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py disagree, the disagreement is the finding: diagnose it rather than overwriting this file to match. The key names are the ones expected/reject-sarif-unresolvable-path.rows.json established, expected/joern.rows.json extended for this tool and expected/reject-sarif-malformed-record.rows.json extended for this condition -- the shared metadata keys, the three parts rows / row_derivations / rejections, and the negative-only additions routing, rejection_boundary, rejections and counts.parse_status -- so one generic loader reads all fifty-two expected files. This is the last of the fifty-two, so it also carries the folder-level reconciliation.
scanner_class_authority: AAP 0.5.4's class table fixes sast for opengrep, semgrep, datadog-static-analyzer and joern. The value is fixed in advance rather than derived from what the artifact turns out to contain, and it is identical on every row. Trivy is the single tool whose scanner_class varies by record, and joern is not it.
rules: No user-specified rule governs this file. review_rules returns exactly one line, 'No user rules provided.', which is the complete document -- read to the end rather than sampled; AAP 0.7 and AAP 0.10.2 say the same. No rule is cited or invented here, and no rule forces this file into scope: it exists because of AAP 0.6.1, AAP 0.6.2 and AAP 0.9.4. Enterprise best practice applies in their place, held to the AAP's own bar: hand-verify from the fixture rather than record a run, verify independently of the thing verified, reject rather than infer, and state an absence rather than omit it. The bar on this file is two things at once -- a rejection class asserted against the module that defines it rather than against the fixture's file name, and an envelope whose four artifact-level measurements two other documents cross-reference, asserted to survive the rejection unchanged and to appear in no row.
artifact_shape_note: This is the only artifact whose shape is the harness's own collector output rather than a tool-native format. There is no Joern output format to look up: harness/bin/run-joern.sh loads the code-property graph with importCpg, runs the bounded query set baked into harness/lib/joern-scan.sc, and that script writes the artifact itself.

fixture.shape: the collector shape the specification documents
fixture.derivation: A negative fixture is derived from captured output rather than being an excerpt of it, so the provenance is stated as a derivation. Two things are derived and nothing else is invented. First, the shape: the raw artifact is written in this provisioning's collector shape, and each well-formed record here is re-spelled into the documented shape -- query_id becomes rule_id, class becomes class_file, the severity label is dropped, and the collector's own path and path_resolution members are supplied. Second, one element of findings[] is replaced by a bare JSON string, which is what the fixture exists to assert. The four class coordinates, their method signatures and their reported lines are all values the raw artifact carries.
fixture.captured_provenance: The four well-formed records are not synthesized. harness/artifacts/raw/joern.json names each of the four class coordinates with the same method signature and the same line: the Master receiveAndReply site at 417, the DriverRunner runCommandWithRetry site at 240, the ProcessBuilderLike anonymous-instance start site at 276, and the OneForOneBlockPusher callback site at 86. The recorded sha256 above is what makes a later edit to the fixture visible: these values are re-derived when the fixture changes, never adjusted to keep a test green.
fixture.why_the_documented_shape_is_the_right_ca: The positive fixture joern.json is in this provisioning's shape, so the documented shape's rule_id, path, class_file, start_line and path_resolution members and its flat cpg_* envelope are unexercised there. Carrying the documented shape here covers that gap at no extra cost, and it is the only shape that carries the flat artifact-level measurements this file's envelope assertions turn on.
fixture.malformed_element_note: The malformed element is the JSON string joern.process-launch-site at index 2 -- deliberately a string that is itself one of the five documented collector rule_id literals. A lenient reader could take it for a rule identifier and manufacture a record around it. It is a non-object, so it is malformed_record and never missing_rule_id, and the resemblance is the trap the choice of literal sets.
fixture.excerpt_note: The fixture is never edited to suit these rows; these rows are re-derived when the fixture changes.

routing.detected_by: normalize.shape -- SARIF is a version of 2.1.0 together with a runs array, and this document carries neither, so it is a native artifact routed by the runner that wrote it
routing.routing_decision: normalize.shape.route for joern returns tool joern, shape native, adapter joern, scanner_class sast
routing.not_a_shape_failure: No shape-detection failure is expected here, and a test asserting one against this fixture would be asserting the wrong thing. The enclosing document is a well-formed native Joern artifact and routes cleanly; exactly one element inside findings[] is not an object, and the adapter rejects that element while still emitting the other four. The fixtures that own shape-detection failure are near-sarif-version-only.json, near-sarif-runs-only.json and unknown-shape.json.
routing.negative_routing_test: The mandated negative routing assertion -- that a native artifact must not route to the SARIF adapter -- belongs to test_shape_routing_negative.py. A Joern artifact is a native artifact, so it is eligible material for that assertion, but the assertion itself is not this file's and is not made here.
routing.caller_fault_is_not_a_rejection: normalize.adapters.joern.JoernAdapterError describes a defective call -- the wrong tool identifier, a relative root, another tool's path base, a path base whose kind is not bytecode_class, a source index that is not one, or a document that is not a mapping -- and stops the caller. None of those is in play here, and none is ever counted as a rejection: a caller fault absorbed into a rejection count would let a wrong root produce a plausible dataset for a whole tool. Note the boundary this fixture sits next to: a document that is not a mapping raises, whereas an ELEMENT of findings[] that is not a mapping is a counted rejection. The container and the record are different scopes.

field_order_authority: harness/lib/normalize/emit.py, the FIELDS constant, which harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py restates as its own FIELDS because AAP 0.6.4 permits an adapter to import paths and severity and nothing else. The two were compared and are identical. Every row below carries all twelve keys in that order, present-with-null rather than omitted.
absence_convention: Absence is JSON null here and in findings.json, and an empty field in findings.csv. tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope are never absent -- exactly emit.REQUIRED_FIELDS, which emit.py derives as the seven fields not in OPTIONAL_FIELDS.

allowlist.note: in_scope is decided by that file alone. The globs are not copied here: the allowlist is the single authority and stays byte-exact. The glob each row matched is recorded per row under row_derivations.

no_absolute_path_in_this_file.statement: No absolute filesystem path appears anywhere in this file, in a row or in prose. AAP 0.8.2: no absolute path is ever emitted. The pinned root is referred to as $SPARK_SRC or as the pinned tree rather than written out, and the fixture's own cpg_path member -- which is absolute in the artifact -- is deliberately not copied.
no_absolute_path_in_this_file.the_one_thing_that_looks_like_one_and_is: Every finding_pointer value below, such as /findings/2, is a JSON Pointer in the sense of RFC 6901 and not a filesystem path. It is stated because a reader checking this claim with a leading-slash grep would otherwise read those pointers as violations.

shape_divergence.summary: This fixture is written in the collector shape the specification documents, which is the opposite half of the divergence expected/joern.rows.json records: that fixture captures this provisioning's shape. The divergence itself is recorded, not repaired -- AAP 0.1.3's authority rule -- and the adapter reads both shapes in a fixed field precedence so the choice is reproducible.
shape_divergence.documented_shape: {tool, cpg_path, generated_at, cpg_methods, cpg_typedecls, source_index_size, declaration_index_size, queries: [{id, count}], findings: [{rule_id, message, path, start_line, method_full_name, class_file, path_resolution}]}
shape_divergence.provisioned_shape: {tool, tool_version, cpg, graph: {methods, type_declarations, files}, query_set, queries: [{id, bound, returned, bound_reached, elapsed_ms, callee_prefixes[]}], findings: [{query_id, severity, message, callee, class, method, file, line}]}

differences.documented: findings[].rule_id, one of five joern. prefixed literals
differences.consequence: Every rule_id below is read from the first candidate of RULE_ID_FIELDS = (rule_id, query_id), so rule_id_from_rule_id counts 4 and rule_id_from_query_id counts 0. Four rather than five: the malformed element never reaches the rule step at all.

differences.documented: findings[].class_file, a class-file path such as org/apache/spark/deploy/master/Master.class
differences.observed_here: findings[].class_file on every well-formed record; no class member is present
differences.consequence: coordinate_from_class_file counts 4 and coordinate_from_class counts 0. The runner metadata names class as record_path_field, so the adapter tries it first and falls through to class_file, which is why a document in either shape resolves. normalize.paths.class_key accepts either form, so the precedence decides which member is read, never how it is interpreted.

differences.observed_here: no severity member at all -- the literal string severity does not occur anywhere in the fixture, checked over the whole document rather than per record
differences.consequence: Every surviving row carries severity_native null and severity_norm Info on the no_vocabulary basis, so severity_absent counts 4 and severity_from_record_label counts 0.
differences.why_this_is_the_contract: AAP 0.5.4 places joern under 'No vocabulary at all (gitleaks; joern unless a query defines one) -- severity_native absent, severity_norm Info, the absence stated rather than a level assumed'. Here no query defines one, so the absence is stated. Info is never written by the adapter directly: severity.py owns the vocabulary, the precedence and the bands, so this file cannot disagree with severity-map.md.

differences.documented: findings[].path, the collector's own already-root-relative answer, and findings[].path_resolution, its explanation of how it got there
differences.observed_here: both present on every well-formed record, and neither present on the malformed element, which carries no members at all
differences.consequence: All four surviving records carry a collector path identical to this run's own unique resolution, so collector_path_corroborated counts 4 while collector_path_used and collector_path_disagreed both count 0. collector_explanation_present also counts 4 -- and here that is four of four well-formed records rather than four of five walked, because the malformed element is rejected before the explanation tally is taken.

differences.documented: flat cpg_methods, cpg_typedecls, source_index_size and declaration_index_size
differences.observed_here: all four present; no nested graph object
differences.consequence: envelope_graph_methods, envelope_graph_type_declarations, envelope_collector_source_index_size and envelope_collector_declaration_index_size all carry figures, while envelope_graph_files stays 0 because the nested object that would supply it is absent. The per-query tally is spelled count here rather than returned, and neither is summed into any published figure.

count_unit.len_findings_includes_the_malformed_elem: Yes, and this is the number to check first. Five is four well-formed records plus the bare string at index 2. normalize.reconcile.count_records reads only the container it needs in order to walk -- the mapping, then the findings array, then its length -- so an element it can make no sense of still counts as one record. An implementation that skipped the unreadable element would report four, the identity would balance against four rows and zero rejections, and the rejection this fixture exists to assert would have vanished without any assertion failing.
count_unit.sum_computed_after_including_the_malform: The two numbers are independent, so the order matters only for how the inequality is read: len(findings) is 5 with the malformed element counted, and the per-query sum is 55 + 178 + 412 + 23 + 24 = 692. The inequality 692 is not equal to 5 therefore holds after the malformed element is included, and holds by a wide margin -- adding one element to a five-element array cannot bring it near a whole scan's tallies.
count_unit.per_query_tally_member: queries[].count in this shape; queries[].returned in the provisioned shape
count_unit.which_one_is_the_raw_count: len(findings) = 5. The sum of the per-query tallies is 692 and is not the raw count and is not published as one.
count_unit.why_they_differ: The fixture carries five findings beside a queries[] array whose counts describe a whole scan. The two numbers therefore differ by construction, which is what makes the reconciliation assertion non-vacuous: an implementation that counted the per-query tallies instead of the findings would produce 692 against 4 rows and 1 rejection and fail loudly rather than agree silently.
count_unit.no_query_to_finding_link: No rule_id is ever taken from a queries[].id. The documented queries[] carries only {id, count} and records no link between a query and a finding, so a match there would be inference; each well-formed finding names its own query through its own rule_id member. The malformed element names none, which is precisely why nothing may be read out of it -- least of all a rule identifier assembled from the queries array.
count_unit.authority: AAP 0.5.4 makes findings[] the reconciliation unit, and normalize.reconcile.count_records walks that same unit without building rows. The adapter deliberately publishes no count of the findings it walked, so the left-hand side of the identity cannot be taken from the traversal that builds the right-hand side.

resolution_context.path_base_source: harness/artifacts/logs/runner-metadata.json, the joern entry's path_base -- read as input, never assumed
resolution_context.why_no_filesystem_base_exists: The runner queries a graph the frontend built over staged JARs rather than over the source tree, so a reported file member is by construction the frontend's extraction path for a class member and can never be a path in the Spark tree. The metadata therefore records a null base value rather than inventing a plausible one, and the class coordinate is the only resolvable one. Because has_explicit_base is false, no metadata-backed fallback is available to this tool at all.
resolution_context.resolution_procedure: The class coordinate is reduced by normalize.paths.class_key to the package path plus the outer type name, truncating the basename at its first dollar sign so a companion object, an anonymous class and a nested class all collapse to the outer type. That key is then looked up in a source index over src/main and src/test under the pinned root, across two key schemes: by_filename on the package directory plus the file base name, and by_decl on the package directory plus each declared type name. The union of candidates must be exactly one distinct path.
resolution_context.gap_1_closed: The index spans src/main and src/test rather than src/main alone. Every -tests artifact the build emitted is in the graph input, so a finding can legitimately name bytecode compiled from a test tree, and such a resolution is retained with in_scope false rather than dropped. No record in this fixture resolves into a test tree, so rows_from_src_test is 0 here.
resolution_context.gap_2_closed: A resolution is taken only where the union of candidates is exactly one distinct path. Two or more is ambiguous_source_resolution with every competing candidate named, never a first-wins pick. Closing gap 1 increases ambiguity, which is why closing gap 2 is mandatory rather than optional.
resolution_context.declaration_scheme_is_not_optional: Row 2 resolves on the declaration scheme alone: no file is named ProcessBuilderLike.scala anywhere in the pinned tree, and DriverRunner.scala is the file that declares the type. Measured rather than argued -- the filename scheme holds no entry for that key at all. A filename-only index would lose that row silently, and a silently lost row is indistinguishable from a class with nothing to report.
resolution_context.collector_explanation_is_a_different_voc: The collector's path_resolution values in this fixture are source-index-filename and source-index-declaration; this run's own bases are source-index-filename+declaration and source-index-declaration. They are not the same vocabulary at the same granularity: this run keys both schemes and reports when both matched, while the collector reports the one scheme it used. Three of the four records therefore carry a collector explanation of source-index-filename against a basis of source-index-filename+declaration. Both are recorded and neither is corrected -- the explanation is evidence about the collector, and normalising it would destroy the thing it is retained for.
resolution_context.collector_path_precedence: Fixed by the adapter and exercised on every well-formed record here. This run's own unique class-to-source resolution governs; an ambiguous key is never overridden by the collector's answer; where this run resolves nothing and the collector did supply a root-relative path, that path is emitted as-is and marked uncorroborated; and where both resolve and differ, this run's answer is kept and the disagreement recorded. All four surviving records take the first branch with the collector agreeing exactly, so collector_path_used is 0.
resolution_context.root_dependence: These rows depend on a live tree: the class-to-source resolution reads the pinned checkout at $SPARK_SRC. Every emitted path is expressed relative to that root and none is absolute. The index figures under counters are the measurement over the pinned tree, and they reproduce the figures the adapter's own docstring records.
resolution_context.severity_source: No record states a severity, and this shape has no rule object to fall back on, so every row takes severity.py's no-vocabulary path: severity_native null, severity_norm Info, basis no_vocabulary. The absence is stated rather than a level assumed.
resolution_context.package_coordinate: null on every row. A Joern finding names a bytecode call site rather than a package, and this shape supplies no coordinate to carry. The absence is explicitly not a rejection: the unformable_package_coordinate class covers a dependency-oriented record, and this shape is not one.

rejection_boundary.statement: A malformed record is a record whose container is not the shape its adapter requires, so nothing can be read out of it with any confidence. It is rejected and counted under malformed_record, never coerced into a row and never dropped. paths.py states the class in one line: the record is not the shape its adapter requires.
rejection_boundary.why_it_can_only_be_a_rejection: Seven of the twelve fields are never absent from a row -- tool, scanner_class, rule_id, message, severity_norm, path and in_scope. An element that is not an object supplies none of them. There is no valid row representation of it, and both alternatives are worse than a rejection: dropping it silently would break the identity raw == rows + rejections, and assembling values for it would put content in the dataset that the artifact does not contain.
rejection_boundary.document_versus_record_scope: This is the property that makes malformed_record a per-record class at all, and it is worth stating because the two failures look alike in a summary and behave nothing alike. A syntactically broken DOCUMENT -- a truncated write, an unbalanced brace -- fails json.load upstream in cli.py, before any record is reached. Nothing is walked, so there is no per-record rejection, no partial parse, no counter and no reconciliation for that artifact: the outcome is a parse failure over the whole file. This fixture is deliberately not that case. Its bytes are well-formed JSON and json.load succeeds, so the walk reaches every one of the five elements and the defect is confined to one of them. No json.load failure is expected here, and a test that asserted one would be exercising the wrong boundary.
rejection_boundary.malformed_element_is_inside_the_count_un: The defective element sits inside findings[], the count unit reconcile.count_records walks, so it is a raw record and the identity has something to prove. Had it been placed outside that array -- a stray key on the envelope, an extra member beside findings -- reconcile would not count it, the arithmetic would still balance, and the fixture would demonstrate nothing about how a defective record is handled.
rejection_boundary.unchecked_access_would_raise: The bare string at /findings/2 is the shape a truncated or mis-serialised producer write actually takes, and it is the shape that defeats unchecked dict-style access. Verified on the fixture's own element rather than asserted: in Python, element[rule_id] on that str raises TypeError with the message that string indices must be integers, and element.get(rule_id) raises AttributeError because a str object has no attribute get. Correct handling turns that raise into a counted rejection rather than a crash, and the crash is the expensive failure -- it would abandon the artifact at element 2 and lose elements 3 and 4 with it. The adapter's own contract is what makes this structural rather than defensive: _adapt_finding narrows the type once, at the top, with _json_object, and returns exactly one of a row or a rejection for every element it is handed.
rejection_boundary.the_position_is_the_point: The element sits at index 2 of 5, mid-array, with two well-formed findings after it. Continuation is therefore the property under test, and it is provable from the row list alone: rows 2 and 3 come from /findings/3 and /findings/4, so a run that stopped, crashed or returned early at element 2 cannot produce these counts. A malformed element in the last position would have satisfied every count in this file while proving none of that.
rejection_boundary.one_string_that_could_have_been_read_as_: The malformed element's text is joern.process-launch-site, which is one of the five documented collector rule_id literals and is the rule_id of two of the surviving rows. It is still a non-object, so it is malformed_record and not missing_rule_id: the class names what the container is, not what its bytes resemble. A permissive implementation that read the string as an identifier would produce a fifth row with no message, no coordinate and no line -- four rejections' worth of missing content in a single row -- and this fixture is where that is caught.

not_a_rejection.case: a finding object whose rule_id is absent, null, empty or a non-string
not_a_rejection.expected: a missing_rule_id rejection, a different class entirely
not_a_rejection.evidence: The adapter keeps the two apart deliberately at steps 1 and 2 of its classification order: an element that is not an object is not shaped like a finding, whereas an object with no identifier is a finding whose producer omitted one, and a reader of tool-status.md acts differently on each.

not_a_rejection.case: a finding object whose message is present but is not a string
not_a_rejection.expected: also malformed_record, but reached at step 3 rather than step 1, and with the record's rule identifier already resolved and counted
not_a_rejection.evidence: Named so the class's full surface is visible rather than implied. It is the route that produces the 4/3 counter asymmetry a reader might expect here and will not find: every well-formed record in this fixture passes steps 2 to 5, so no counter splits.

not_a_rejection.case: a coordinate that resolves into a src/test tree, from a -tests artifact in the graph input
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope and rows_from_src_test
not_a_rejection.evidence: AAP 0.5.4 requires a test-JAR finding kept out of scope rather than dropped, and AAP 0.9.3 repeats it among the recorded-not-halting conditions. The literal src/test exclusion lives in paths.in_scope and removes the path from scope, never from the dataset.

not_a_rejection.case: a coordinate that resolves outside the twelve authoritative globs
not_a_rejection.expected: a kept row with in_scope false, counted under rows_out_of_scope
not_a_rejection.evidence: A class in a module the allowlist does not name resolves to a real file and is kept. Out of scope means kept and marked. All four rows here match a glob, so rows_out_of_scope is 0.

rejection_boundary.no_guessed_field: The rejected element is given no rule identifier, no message, no path and no line. Its rejection carries only what identifies it in the artifact -- its index in findings[] -- so the record can be found again without any content being invented for it. There is nothing else to carry: the element has no members.

counts.raw_count_unit: one element of findings[] -- the unit normalize.reconcile.count_records walks independently of row construction
counts.raw_count_authority: normalize.reconcile.count_records for joern, whose traversal takes the length of the findings array and builds no row, resolves no path and maps no severity. It is the independent half of the identity: a count taken from the traversal that builds the rows would satisfy the assertion while testing nothing. Measured on this fixture, it returns 5.
counts.raw_count_includes_the_malformed_element: Yes. Five is four well-formed records plus the bare string at index 2, and the inequality against the per-query tallies is computed with it included -- 692 is not equal to 5. See count_unit for both figures and why the traversal counts an element it cannot read.
counts.rejections_by_class_completeness: One class, one record. The other nine members of paths.REJECT_CLASSES count zero for this fixture, and an assertion should compare against the class name rather than against the rejection count alone: a test that only counts rejections cannot tell one condition from another, and every one of the six reject-joern-* fixtures produces at least one rejection.
counts.one_finding_one_outcome: Structural rather than asserted: the adapter's per-finding function returns a single value that is either a row or a rejection, so there is no path that emits both and none that emits neither. len(rows) + len(rejections) therefore equals the number of findings[] elements walked by construction.

four_reported_counters.authority: AAP 0.5.4 -- the four counts reported per tool
four_reported_counters.values_live_in: counters, for the two this adapter publishes, and aap_reported_counters for all four with the reason each is what it is

counts.parse_status_authority: harness/lib/normalize/cli.py, PARSE_STATUS_PARTIAL = partial, assigned where there are rejections and clean where there are none. Partial is right precisely because the adapter did not abandon the artifact: every parsable record was emitted and the one rejected record is counted under its class, with its reason retained verbatim. This is deliberately not normalize.reconcile's pass / fail / not_applicable vocabulary, which describes an assertion's outcome rather than an artifact's parse.
counts.not_applicable_is_a_different_case: An artifact that was never written reconciles as not applicable -- artifact absent, not as zero equals zero. That case belongs to osv-scanner, which wrote nothing, and it is not this fixture's.

counters_authority: harness/lib/normalize/adapters/joern.py, COUNTER_KEYS as returned by new_counters(): 43 keys -- 23 authored, 5 envelope integers, one path_kind_* per normalize.paths.PATH_KINDS member, one severity_basis_* per normalize.severity.BASIS_VALUES member, and one provenance key per member of each field-candidate tuple. The keys above are in COUNTER_KEYS order and the set is complete: every key the adapter initialises appears, so a zero here means measured-zero rather than not-measured.
counters_note: Four things a reader must not correct. First, and this is the one that distinguishes this fixture from its unresolvable-path sibling: NO counter splits. Every per-finding counter reads 4 rather than 5 and none reads 3, because the malformed element is rejected at step 1 -- before the record's identity context is gathered, before the rule identifier is read, before the coordinate member is chosen and before the collector-explanation tally is taken. It contributes to no counter at all. The sibling reject-joern-unresolvable-path fixture splits 4 / 3 precisely because its defective record passes steps 1 to 3 first; here there is nothing to split, and a reader expecting the asymmetry should read the classification order rather than adjust these numbers. Second, envelope_graph_files is 0 while the four other envelope figures carry values: this shape has no nested graph object, so the member that would supply a file count is absent, and 0 here means absent rather than a graph with no files. Third, source_index_supplied is 0, recording that the adapter built the index over the pinned root rather than being handed one; a test injecting a synthetic index changes exactly the seven source_index_* keys and nothing else. Fourth, source_index_ambiguous_by_filename is 4 and source_index_ambiguous_by_decl is 107 -- ambiguity measured in the index, not encountered by this fixture. No coordinate here hits an ambiguous key, so no record is rejected for it; reject-joern-ambiguous-path.json is the fixture that does.

aap_reported_counters.note: AAP 0.5.4 has four counters reported per tool. Two are members of this adapter's COUNTER_KEYS and two are not, and the reason the two are absent is structural rather than an omission.

multi_location_records.basis: No finding in this shape carries a locations array; each names exactly one call site through its class coordinate, its method and its line. The malformed element carries no members at all, so it cannot carry one either. The counter is published anyway, so that a future collector emitting several locations is visible rather than silently reduced to its first.

non_filesystem_paths.basis: All four emitted paths have kind bytecode_source, which normalize.paths.is_non_filesystem_kind excludes -- only outside_root and archive_member are non-filesystem coordinates. Each names a real file in the pinned tree. The rejected element contributes to no path_kind_* counter at all, because it produced no row.

multi_valued_cwe_records.basis: Not a member of this adapter's COUNTER_KEYS; the SARIF adapter publishes it because a SARIF rule can carry several CWE tokens. A Joern finding names a bytecode call site rather than a weakness catalogue entry, so cwe is null on every row by contract and the count is structurally 0. Manufacturing a CWE from a class name or a query identifier would be inference.

multi_valued_cve_records.basis: Not a member of this adapter's COUNTER_KEYS, for the same reason: this shape carries no advisory identifier, so cve is null on every row by contract and the count is structurally 0.

envelope_fields.note: The envelope members outside findings[] are not findings and produce no rows. They must not appear in any row, and a twelve-key row makes that structural. They are recorded here because they are the figures a reader checks the artifact's provenance against, and a number that reaches no channel reaches no document.
envelope_fields.graph_figures_agree_with_the_run_record: cpg_methods 1397339 and cpg_typedecls 119691 are the figures recorded for the graph this run queried, so a fixture whose envelope disagreed with them would be a fixture built against a different graph. They are carried as evidence of provenance and are compared, never summed into a record count.
envelope_fields.collector_index_sizes_do_not_coincide_he: source_index_size 4127 and declaration_index_size 9944 are the collector's own reported index sizes, and unlike the sibling fixture's they do NOT coincide with this run's independently measured source index of 6759 files and 15230 declaration keys. Both figures are recorded with both provenances and neither is adjusted to make them agree: the collector's number is a fact about the collector, this run's is a fact about the index this run built, and a difference between two measurements is a difference to record rather than a discrepancy to repair. The difference has no effect on any row, because no path below is resolved through the collector's index.
envelope_fields.cpg_path_member: The envelope carries a cpg_path member naming the graph file. It is an absolute path in the artifact and is deliberately not copied into this file, which stays free of absolute paths; the graph's identity is recorded elsewhere by byte size and sha256.
envelope_fields.generated_at_member: The fixture carries generated_at and it is deliberately not asserted: it is a timestamp, it reaches no dataset field, and pinning it would make this file fail for a reason that has nothing to do with the adapter.
envelope_fields.bound_reached: This shape's queries[] carries only {id, count} and no bound_reached flag, so no query can report reaching a traversal bound and the counter is 0. That is the flag being absent rather than a query being known untruncated, and the two are not the same claim.

envelope_survives_the_rejection.why_this_check_belongs_to_this_fixture_a: Joern's artifact is the only one of the nine that carries artifact-level MEASUREMENTS in its envelope -- cpg_methods, cpg_typedecls, source_index_size and declaration_index_size. The other four malformed-record fixtures (sarif, trivy, checkov, gitleaks, dependency-check) carry no equivalent, so for them a record-level failure can only cost a row. Here it could cost a cross-DOCUMENT check: oss-scan-results/build-record.md and oss-scan-results/run-record.md both cross-reference the graph's method and type-declaration figures, and a failure path that discarded or corrupted the envelope while recovering from the malformed record would break that agreement rather than merely lose a row. So this fixture asserts the envelope as well as the rows.
envelope_survives_the_rejection.survive_unchanged: All four are expected byte-for-byte as the fixture states them, with no coercion and no default. The adapter reads them in _record_envelope BEFORE it walks findings[] at all, and a non-integer or negative value is skipped rather than coerced, so a record-level rejection inside the walk cannot reach them. Their surfacing under the envelope_ prefix in counters is the only channel they take: envelope_graph_methods 1397339, envelope_graph_type_declarations 119691, envelope_collector_source_index_size 4127, envelope_collector_declaration_index_size 9944.
envelope_survives_the_rejection.survive_readable: Readable as well as unchanged: each of the four is an integer in the fixture and an integer in the counter, so a consumer of tool-status.md can compare it against the run record without parsing a string. envelope_graph_files is the one envelope counter at 0, and it is 0 because the nested graph object that would supply a file count is absent from this shape -- absent rather than zero-valued.
envelope_survives_the_rejection.appear_in_no_row: None of the four is a dataset field, and none appears in any field of any row. The twelve-key row makes it structural rather than a matter of care: there is no key for a graph measurement to occupy. Checked by comparing each value's decimal text against every field of every row rather than by inspection.
envelope_survives_the_rejection.not_a_record_count: The four are evidence of provenance, never a count of anything the reconciliation uses. AAP 0.5.4 makes findings[] the reconciliation unit, so an envelope figure -- like the per-query tally -- is deliberately excluded from the left-hand side of raw == rows + rejections. Substituting one would satisfy no assertion here and would quietly replace the independent count the identity depends on.

independent_derivation.method: Every field of every row, the rejection's class and its full detail string, its record identity and all 43 counter values were derived by reading the fixture against the authored contracts in harness/lib/normalize/ -- emit.FIELDS for the field set and order, paths.REJECT_CLASSES for the class name, the adapter's documented five-step classification order for the step the defective element is decided at, and severity.py's no-vocabulary path for the severity triple. The class keys were reduced by hand under class_key's documented first-dollar-sign truncation and looked up against a source index measured over the pinned tree. The four line anchors were checked by reading the pinned files themselves.
independent_derivation.index_measurement: 6759 files indexed, 6755 by_filename keys of which 4 are ambiguous, and 15230 by_decl keys of which 107 are ambiguous -- reproducing the figures the adapter's own docstring records.

members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.note: Each of these is present in the fixture and must not appear in any row. Checked by substring comparison against every field of every row above, not merely by inspection.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.path_resolution: The collector's own explanation of how it resolved a class, one of source-index-filename, source-index-declaration or unresolved-bytecode-only. AAP 0.5.4 confines it to the rejection record: any collector explanation for an unmappable bytecode path is retained in the rejection record, not in a dataset field. It is diagnostic metadata, not data. Two of the three literals occur in this fixture -- source-index-filename and source-index-declaration -- and neither occurs anywhere in the rows array. The third, unresolved-bytecode-only, occurs nowhere in this fixture at all, because no record here fails to resolve.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.method_full_name: The enclosing method's full signature, carried by all four well-formed records. It reaches a rejection's identity as diagnosable context and never a row -- and never message, however readable it looks. The malformed element carries none, which is why this fixture's rejection identity has only one key.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.envelope_members: tool, cpg_path, generated_at, cpg_methods, cpg_typedecls, source_index_size, declaration_index_size and queries are envelope metadata: not findings, and they produce no rows. The four measurements among them are asserted separately under envelope_survives_the_rejection.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.the_malformed_element_itself: The string joern.process-launch-site is the malformed element's entire content, and it reaches no dataset field either. It does occur as the rule_id of rows 1 and 2 -- read from those records' own rule_id members, at /findings/1/rule_id and /findings/3/rule_id -- so a test asserting the malformed element's text is absent from the rows would be asserting something false. The correct assertion is by position: no row derives from /findings/2, which the finding_pointer values above make checkable.
members_that_reach_no_dataset_field.collector_path_is_the_exception_that_is_: findings[].path does reach the path field, but only as a value the adapter may emit as-is when this run's own resolution produces nothing unique -- and on this fixture it never does that, because all four records that resolve use their own resolution. So no row's path came from the collector here, which the counters record as collector_path_used 0.

rejections.locator_note: The pointer and finding_index name the same record. finding_index is carried as well because normalize.adapters.joern puts exactly that key into the rejection's record_identity, so a produced Rejection and this expectation can be compared directly without translating one coordinate system into the other. It is the native-shape equivalent of the run_index / result_index pair the SARIF expectations carry, and for this fixture it is the ONLY identity key there is.
rejections.reject_class_authority: harness/lib/normalize/paths.py, the REJECT_MALFORMED_RECORD constant -- a literal member of paths.REJECT_CLASSES, the closed set of ten, and the tenth and last of them. Written verbatim rather than paraphrased, and asserted against the module rather than by eye: a test that only counts rejections cannot tell one condition from another, so the class name is what carries the assertion.
rejections.element_value_note: Recorded because it is the reason a lenient implementation would fail here rather than elsewhere: the string is itself one of the five documented collector rule_id literals. It is not a secret, a credential or a token -- it is a query identifier -- so recording it verbatim carries nothing sensitive into git.
rejections.classification_step: step 1 of the adapter's fixed classification order -- shape, rule identifier, message, path, start_line. The element is not a JSON object, so _json_object returns None and the rejection is returned before anything else is read. Steps 2 to 5 are never reached.
rejections.nothing_is_read_before_the_rejection: This is what separates this fixture from every other reject-joern-* fixture, and it is visible in the counters rather than merely asserted. Because the rejection is returned at step 1, the element contributes to NO counter at all: not rule_id_from_rule_id, not coordinate_from_class_file, not collector_explanation_present, not start_line_from_start_line, not any severity, path_kind or in_scope counter. Every per-finding counter therefore reads 4 -- one per well-formed record -- and none reads 3. The record's identity context is not gathered either, because the CONTEXT_FIELDS loop runs after the shape guard.
rejections.expected_detail: the findings element is a str, not an object, so no finding can be read from it
rejections.expected_detail_note: The detail is the sub-reason AAP 0.5.4 requires a rejection to carry, retained verbatim as the adapter builds it -- the findings array's member name, the observed Python type name, and why nothing can be read. It is quoted in full because malformed_record covers several routes: naming the class alone would not distinguish an element that is not an object from an object whose message is of the wrong type or whose location chain is malformed. A test may assert the class exactly and the detail by full-string equality here, since the detail carries no measured value that could legitimately change.
rejections.record_identity_note: Exactly one key, and that is the expected shape rather than a shortfall. The adapter supplies finding_index at the shape guard and adds the context members and the rule identifier only after the element has been established as an object; a non-object carries no members to add. Enough to find the element in the artifact again, and never the element's content beyond the type that made it defective.
rejections.why_not_a_row: There is nothing to build a row from. Seven of the twelve fields are never absent, and a non-object element supplies none of them -- no rule identifier, no message, no coordinate, no line. The alternatives are worse: dropping it would break raw == rows + rejections silently, and assembling a row around the one string it does carry would put a rule identifier in the dataset that no finding claimed.
rejections.contributes_no_severity_literal: The rejected element is never fed to the severity tally, so nothing from it reaches severity-map.md. That document reports literals against the rows the dataset contains, and this element contributes none. It carries no severity literal in any case, and neither does any well-formed record in this fixture.
rejections.contributes_no_path_kind: The element produced no path, so it contributes to no path_kind_* counter and to non_filesystem_paths not at all -- and unlike the unresolvable-path sibling's rejected record, it contributes to no earlier-step counter either.

joern_negative_set.coverage_observation: Of those seven, six are named by a fixture in this set. absent_path is named by none: the adapter reaches it through a finding with no class member at all, or one carrying the collector's <unknown> sentinel -- written where a method has no enclosing type declaration, and classified as an absent coordinate rather than an unresolvable one because keying an index on that literal would turn a stated absence into an ordinary lookup miss. Recorded as an observation about the set rather than resolved here, since adding a fixture is not this file's to do and a coverage gap nobody wrote down is a coverage gap nobody checks. expected/reject-joern-unresolvable-path.rows.json records the same gap from its own side, and the two agree.

conditions_this_adapter_cannot_produce.condition: a uriBaseId fault -- a base absent from originalUriBaseIds, a chain that cycles, a chain beyond the fixed depth, a degenerate base, or a chain terminating on a relative reference with no absolute ancestor
reject_classes_involved: unresolvable_path (by the SARIF route, with the sub-reason in the detail)
conditions_this_adapter_cannot_produce.why_unreachable_here: The bounded chain walk is a property of SARIF's uri plus uriBaseId plus run.originalUriBaseIds structure. A Joern finding carries a bytecode class coordinate and no URI at all, so there is no base to look up and no chain to walk. Measurably so for the class-level consequence: the literal INVALID_URI does not occur anywhere in adapters/joern.py, so invalid_uri is unreachable from this adapter -- while joern does reach unresolvable_path by an entirely different route, a class key with zero candidates.

conditions_this_adapter_cannot_produce.produced_by: the dependency-oriented adapters -- trivy and dependency-check, and osv-scanner had it written an artifact
conditions_this_adapter_cannot_produce.why_unreachable_here: Joern records are not dependency-oriented. A finding names a bytecode call site rather than a package, so package_coordinate is null on every row this adapter emits, by the field-source table rather than by accident. A field that is never formed cannot fail to form, so the condition has no route into this adapter -- and the null is explicitly not a rejection.

conditions_this_adapter_cannot_produce.condition: a record that cannot be attributed to a section
conditions_this_adapter_cannot_produce.why_unreachable_here: Sections are a structure of a Trivy report -- Vulnerabilities, Secrets and Misconfigurations under one Results entry -- and a record's scanner_class is derived from which of them it was read from. The Joern shape has no equivalent: scanner_class is sast for every row, fixed per tool in advance by AAP 0.5.4's class table, so there is nothing to fail to attribute.

joern_negative_set.absence_reads_as_a_decision: Those three are named so their absence from the reject-joern-* set is legible as a property of the Joern shape rather than as three fixtures somebody forgot. Seven producible plus three unreachable is the closed set of ten in paths.REJECT_CLASSES, so the accounting is complete.

prohibitions_observed.no_secret_value: No field in this file carries a secret, a credential or a token. The fixture is Joern query output over bytecode call sites and contains none; the rejection carries one array index and, as context, the query identifier that was the malformed element's entire text -- a rule name, not a value. Nothing that could be a credential is recorded, here or in any row, and this file is committed to git.
prohibitions_observed.no_cross_tool_interpretation: One tool is named, joern, in each row's tool field. The sibling fixtures, adapters and expected files referenced above are named to place this fixture in its set and to say which file owns which condition -- never to compare what any tool found, to rank coverage, or to explain why one tool reported something another did not. The three conditions named as unreachable here are named by their structural cause and their owning fixture, which is an accounting of the closed rejection-class set rather than a comparison of tools.
prohibitions_observed.no_deduplication: Nothing here is merged. Rows 1 and 2 resolve to the same file at different lines and are two rows; two identical findings from one tool would likewise be two rows, and two tools reporting one location would be two rows and no comment.
prohibitions_observed.no_judgement: No surviving row is characterised as real, important, a false positive or a duplicate, and the rejected element is not characterised as a tool defect. A rejection is a statement about what could be read out of a record, not about whether the finding was worth reporting. The anchor notes describe what is at each line so the line is checkable; they do not assess the code.
prohibitions_observed.single_artifact_scope: This file describes exactly one artifact -- harness/artifacts/raw/joern.json, as re-spelled into the documented shape by its fixture -- and draws on nothing else. No Joern output written anywhere other than harness/artifacts/raw/ contributes a value here, a row, or a record to any count, because only that tree's artifacts reach the dataset and folding in anything else would corrupt both this tool's count and the dataset's total.
prohibitions_observed.no_absolute_path: See no_absolute_path_in_this_file above: none is emitted, the pinned root is named rather than written, the fixture's absolute cpg_path is not copied, and the only leading-slash values are JSON Pointers.
